a:r.a:t: Accelerated Evolution Identified in Regulatory Sequences

p:cNvPr.descr: The HAR1F locus (labeled upper left) is shown compared among several species. The species are listed along the left side of the diagram. They are, from top to bottom: human, chimpanzee, gorilla, orangutan, macaque, mouse, dog, cow, platypus, opossum, and chicken. The top horizontal axis is labeled “position” and the range is 10 to 60, with interval 10. There is a small key at the bottom showing the meaning of the shadings of the substitutions. A green shading indicates a compensatory mutation, while an orange shading indicates a non-compensatory mutation. The sequence is generally the same between species but with a high number of substitutions for humans. The substituted nucleotides will be indicated by the color they are shaded within the sequence. For humans, the sequence is: AGAC(green)G(green)TTACAGCAAC(green)G(green)TG(orange)TCAG(orange)CTGAAATG(orange)ATG(green)GGC(green)TAGACG(green)CAC(green)GT. The sequence for chimpanzees is AGAAATTACAGCAATTTATCAACTGAAATTATAGGTGTGTAGACACATGT. The same sequence is seen for gorillas, orangutans, opossums, chickens, and dogs. Macaques, mice, and cows all have a single substitution at nucleotide 33, which originally was an A but has been changed to G and highlighted orange. Cows also have an additional substitution at nucleotide 28, which was initially T but was changed to C (orange). The platypus has two substitutions, one at nucleotide 12 which was G but was changed to T (green) and one at nucleotide 35 which was C but was changed to A (green).
